sections.overview: The Tundra Swan is an Arctic-breeding swan whose North American populations winter along both Pacific and Atlantic flyways.
sections.identification: The bill is mostly black with a variable yellow mark; Eurasian Bewick’s Swans usually show more yellow than North American birds.
sections.habitat: It breeds on wet Arctic tundra near lakes and rivers, then uses lakes, marshes, estuaries and sometimes fields during migration and winter.
sections.diet: In summer it grazes aquatic vegetation; on migration and wintering grounds it also feeds on leftover crops and winter cereals.
sections.behavior: Families migrate together, while breeding birds form pairs that defend nesting territories and generally remain paired across years.
sections.reproduction: Both parents build a mound of vegetation near water, and the female lays a clutch of several eggs.
sections.ecology: The species includes the North American columbianus and Eurasian bewickii forms in many taxonomies; compare the catalogue’s Mute Swan and Whooper Swan profiles.
sections.conservation: Canada’s 2025 report estimated 77 200 birds in the eastern population and 72 900 in the western population.
